paragraph: PROPHET IN ISRAEL AFTER ELIJAH, FROM THE DAYS OF JORAM TO THE DAYS OF JOASH · TWO KINGDOMS

blocks.text: PROPHET IN ISRAEL AFTER ELIJAH, FROM THE DAYS OF JORAM TO THE DAYS OF JOASH · TWO KINGDOMS
Elisha. Called from the plough by Elijah's mantle; “the man of God” of Shunem, Naaman and the siege of Samaria.
Joram · “The king of Israel” of 2 Kings 5–8 · Jehoshaphat · Ben-hadad · Hazael · Jehu · Jehoash
The mantle at the plough (1 Kings 19:16–21)
Called, as two accounts tell it
“Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.”

Many of his words carry “Thus saith the LORD”: over the spring at Jericho, to the three kings, over the twenty loaves, and to the starving city of Samaria. 2 Kings 2:21 2 Kings 3:16–17 2 Kings 4:43 2 Kings 7:1
Before he answered the three kings he asked for a minstrel, “and it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him”. 2 Kings 3:15

He knew what happened out of sight: Gehazi's errand (“Went not mine heart with thee”), the Syrian king's words “in thy bedchamber”, and the king's messenger coming to take his head. 2 Kings 5:26 2 Kings 6:9–12 2 Kings 6:32
He also said when something had been hidden from him: of the Shunammite's grief, “the LORD hath hid it from me, and hath not told me”. 2 Kings 4:27
He spoke of what “the LORD hath shewed me” about Ben-hadad and Hazael, and prayed that his servant's eyes be opened to see the horses and chariots of fire. 2 Kings 8:10 2 Kings 8:13 2 Kings 6:17

He used things at hand: salt in a new cruse, meal in the pot, a stick cast in the water, and arrows shot from a window. His staff, laid on the dead child's face by Gehazi, did not wake him. 2 Kings 2:20–21 2 Kings 4:29–31 2 Kings 4:41 2 Kings 6:6 2 Kings 13:15–18
“What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother.”
“The king of Israel” of 2 Kings 5–8 (not named)
“See ye how this son of a murderer hath sent to take away mine head?”
“were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee.”
KING OF SYRIA (ARAM) IN THE DAYS OF ELISHA
“Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the LORD hath shewed me that he shall surely die.”
“Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel”
“Thus saith the LORD, I have anointed thee king over Israel.”
“The arrow of the LORD’s deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria”
The word in its main themes
“let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
“Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel”
Deliverance from Moab and from Syria
“this is but a light thing in the sight of the LORD: he will deliver the Moabites also into your hand.”
“As the LORD liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none.”
“set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.”
“the LORD hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years.”
To whom the word was spoken
“Thus saith the LORD, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.”
“Thus saith the LORD, Make this valley full of ditches.”
TO A WIDOW OF THE SONS OF THE PROPHETS
“Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.”
“About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son.”
“Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.”
“The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever.”
“Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.”
“Thou shalt not smite them: wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow?”
“To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.”
TO THE LORD ON WHOSE HAND THE KING LEANED
“Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.”
“The LORD hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.”
“Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times; then hadst thou smitten Syria till thou hadst consumed it: whereas now thou shalt smite Syria but thrice.”
Twenty loaves for a hundred men
Horses and chariots of fire at Dothan
Who stood with him, and against him
The site's record for the people of Shunem
The lord on whose hand the king leaned

“Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died.” Joash king of Israel came down and wept over him, “O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof”, the words Elisha had cried when Elijah was taken. 2 Kings 13:14 2 Kings 2:12
“And Elisha died, and they buried him.” 2 Kings 13:20
When a dead man was cast into his sepulchre and touched his bones, “he revived, and stood up on his feet”. 2 Kings 13:21
Jesus said in Nazareth, “many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Luke 4:27
From the textKings does not say where he was buried or how old he was. 2 Kings 13:20

Ecclesiasticus says “Eliseus was filled with his spirit”, that “he was not moved with the presence of any prince”, and that “after his death his body prophesied”. Sirach 48:12–14 [9] Who says so: Jesus son of Sirach, Ecclesiasticus 48 (KJV Apocrypha), about 200 BC on T. W. Davies's dating; scholars differ

Jerome writes that at Samaria, renamed Sebaste, “There lie the prophets Elisha and Obadiah and John the Baptist”.[14] Who says so: Jerome, Letter 108 (to Eustochium) 13, written after Paula's death in AD 404
C. F. Keil (tr. 1872), pp. 292–293, following Levi ben Gershom, Grotius and Hengstenberg

Keil bases the request on Deuteronomy 21:17, where the firstborn receives a double portion of his father's inheritance: Elisha asked, as Elijah's firstborn among the sons of the prophets, for the heir's share of his spirit. 2 Kings 2:9 Deuteronomy 21:17 [1]
Translators from Ephraem Syrus to Köster and F. W. Krummacher, Luther following the Vulgate; J. Le Clerc and A. Pfeiffer on Elisha's miracles (as reported, and rejected, by Keil, pp. 292–293)
Keil reports that many took it as a double measure of Elijah's spirit, some pointing to Elisha's many and greater miracles, and answers that the words do not mean this. 2 Kings 2:9–10 [1]
1 Kings 19 2 Kings 2 2 Kings 3 2 Kings 4 2 Kings 5 2 Kings 6 2 Kings 7 2 Kings 8 2 Kings 9 2 Kings 13 Luke 4
1 Kings 19:16–21 2 Kings 2:1–25 2 Kings 3:9–27 2 Kings 4:1–44 2 Kings 5:1–27 2 Kings 6:1–33 2 Kings 7:1–20 2 Kings 8:1–15 2 Kings 9:1–11 2 Kings 13:14–25 Luke 4:27
Scripture does not name the king of Israel in 2 Kings 5–8, the king of Syria in Naaman's story, or the Shunammite woman.
Kings does not give Elisha's age, or say where he was buried.
Scripture does not explain how Gehazi, after his leprosy, was talking with the king in 2 Kings 8:4–5.
Kings does not say whether Elisha ever met Jehu; the anointing was done by the young prophet he sent.
Elisha wrote no book, and Scripture records no writing of his.
